api_doc_gaps.endpoint: RULE-SEC-005 / QR-SEC-031 — where a "module-declared conflicting pair" is declared
api_doc_gaps.detail: RULE-SEC-005 and QR-SEC-031 both hinge on two actions being declared a conflicting pair by their owning module, but no SEC v1 artifact says where that declaration lives: there is no ENT, no DBF, no table and no API for it (db-script-sec.md §1 has 104 DBF across 13 tables, none of them a conflict register; srs-sec.md A3 lists no such entity). QR-SEC-031 is therefore implementable only as "does this user already hold action X", with X supplied from outside SEC.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: ABSENT, resolved without inventing a contract (orchestrate-module STEP 2 step 5, after the STEP 1.4 second-agent debate). Findings: (a) SEC v1 declares no conflicting-pair source anywhere — srs-sec.md A3 entities, A6 lookups, A7 defaults/state machines, A8 cross-module, Part B screens B3/B5, §7.1 permissions, db-script-sec.md's 104 DBF across 13 tables, and API-SEC-020's action-registration request contract were all checked and are empty; (b) REQ-SEC-020 is `Pattern : optional` — "Where a consumer module declares two of its actions as conflicting" — an EARS precondition SEC v1 never establishes; (c) the platform's only real conflicting pair is FIN-owned and FIN-enforced, not SEC-enforced: governance/modules/FIN/P3_1/backend-execution-plan-fin.md:1061-1066 states PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE and PERM_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_CREATE are separated "by platform convention (an administrative guideline enforced by role design, not a database constraint — SEC's RBAC model grants permissions per role, and FIN's service layer additionally checks at hard-close/year-end-close time that no single user holds both, per role union)", and :383-386 adds that this check "runs in FIN's own service layer by reading the two roles' user sets through SEC's role/grant read APIs'. Corroborated: RULE-FIN-015 (srs-fin.md:1012) is scoped to ENT-FIN-008 with trigger "on evaluate (period-close-approval action)", and FIN carries its own error code FIN-403-SOD-VIOLATION (403) for it — no FIN-owned P1/P2/P3_1 artifact ever routes through SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT. Consequence for SVC-API: API-SEC-008 / API-SEC-017 are implemented as their Orchestration lines read, with the RULE-SEC-005 step driven by a conflicting-counterpart set that is EMPTY in SEC v1 (a private service-side resolver returning empty), so the DATA-DOM guards and both QR-SEC-031 methods keep a real caller and A.2.9 holds at ALIGN-BE. No table, column, route, error code or rule is invented. Remaining human-only question (a P1/P2 amendment, not an execution decision): whether SEC v1 should own a conflicting-pair register at all, rather than leaving REQ-SEC-020's precondition permanently unestablished. Aligned 2026-09-11: the deferral is now recorded at its own sites — a Note field on REQ-SEC-020 and on RULE-SEC-005 in governance/modules/SEC/P1/srs-sec.md, and a DEFERRED (SEC v1) clause on the RULE-SEC-005 line in governance/modules/SEC/P3_1/backend-execution-plan-sec.md and packages/backend-execution/DATA-DOM/DATA-DOM-TRANSACTIONAL.md; no register, table, field or API was invented.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: [PATCH] /api/v1/sec/signup-requests/{id} — created User.passwordHash (DBF-SEC-004)
api_doc_gaps.detail: DBF-SEC-004 password_hash is NOT NULL (db-script-sec.md §1 registry row / §3 CREATE TABLE SEC_USER), but no artifact says what credential an approved sign-up account receives. API-SEC-011's Orchestration line reads "on APPROVE: create User (QR-SEC-006-style, statusCode=ACTIVE) + update SignupRequest (statusCode=APPROVED, reviewedBy/At) (QR-SEC-011)" and names no password, hash or token; srs-sec.md REQ-SEC-004 ("the system shall create an active user account from it") and AC-SEC-004 ("the system creates a User with status ACTIVE from its email/name, and marks the SignupRequest APPROVED") specify only email and name; REQ-SEC-005 is the symmetric negative path and creates nothing. The sign-up request body itself (API-SEC-002: {email, fullNameAr, fullNameEn}) carries no password, and ENT-SEC-013's FIELDS table (DBF-SEC-097..104) has no credential column, so there is nothing to carry forward at approval time.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: Implementation choice filling a spec silence, grounded rather than invented: the account is created with passwordEncoder.encode(UUID.randomUUID().toString()) — an unusable secret that is never logged, transmitted or returned, so the account exists and is ACTIVE but cannot be authenticated against until a real credential is set. The artifact-grounded path for the owner to obtain one is the existing API-SEC-003 (request password reset) → API-SEC-004 (complete password reset) pair, governed by RULE-SEC-006 and already specified in SVC-API-INT.md; no new endpoint, column, error code or rule was created, and no cross-module call was added (SEC is ROOT, zero XM). Note that no SEC artifact states the approved user is notified or that a reset token is issued automatically on approval — see the SVC-API-CRUD report finding — so as specified the account is reachable only after someone informs its owner out of band. Whether SEC v1 should define an approval-time credential or notification step is a P1/P2 amendment for a human, not an execution decision. Aligned 2026-09-11: the implemented credential behaviour, the API-SEC-003 → API-SEC-004 route in, and the unresolved notification silence are now recorded as a Notes line on API-SEC-011 in governance/modules/SEC/P3_1/backend-execution-plan-sec.md and packages/backend-execution/SVC-API/SVC-API-CRUD.md, and as a Note field on REQ-SEC-004 in governance/modules/SEC/P1/srs-sec.md; both candidate answers are stated, neither chosen.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: [POST] /api/v1/sec/auth/password-reset/request — REQ-SEC-029 NOTIF dispatch from a pre-authentication caller
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-SEC-003 is public / pre-authentication (Security line: "screen SEC_PWD_RESET · public — no permission required"), but the only sanctioned consuming surface, com.erp.notif.crossmodule.NotificationDispatchApi, delegates to NOTIF's DispatchService.dispatch, whose declared contract is @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()") (NotificationDispatchApiImpl javadoc: "Authorization is enforced on the delegate (@PreAuthorize isAuthenticated(), SEC-BE)"; the annotation itself is currently present on DispatchService.dispatch while the per-method SEC gates elsewhere in notif sit behind "// TODO: SEC-PENDING" comments). Once SEC-BE activates that gate for every call path, an anonymous password-reset request will be denied at the dispatch call. build-create-service's "Internal trusted-caller calls" section describes the sanctioned fix — a synthetic authentication carrying a dedicated internal authority, installed by the project's internal-caller utility — but NO such utility exists in this repository, and no SEC or NOTIF artifact names an authority, a bridge or an exemption for a pre-authentication caller. Adjacent fact at the same call site: NOTIF's dispatch is @Transactional with default REQUIRED propagation, so it JOINS SEC's READ_WRITE transaction; a failure raised inside that advice (e.g. an unknown template code) marks the shared transaction rollback-only, which a consuming-side try/catch cannot undo. An AccessDeniedException from @PreAuthorize is raised before the transaction advice and is therefore genuinely survivable; a failure inside doDispatch is not.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: CLOSED 2026-09-11 — both halves. (1) AUTHORIZATION HALF, closed at SEC-BE by the sanctioned internal-caller pattern and nothing else: com.erp.sec.security.InternalCallerContext.call(..) installs a synthetic UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken (principal "internal") carrying exactly one authority, INTERNAL_TRUSTED_CALLER, for the duration of the call and restores the previous SecurityContext in a finally block; PasswordResetService.dispatchResetNotification wraps only the crossmodule call site in it, inside the pre-existing catch-and-log, so REQ-SEC-006 still answers its generic 200 when Notifications is unavailable. The authority cannot be obtained externally: JwtAuthenticationFilter is the single authentication entry point and strips INTERNAL_TRUSTED_CALLER from every authority set it builds. Still deferred, with reason: build-create-service also prescribes a build-time ArchUnit guard that no @RestController/@Controller reaches the gated method; it was NOT written because governance/GOVERNANCE-RULES.md forbids creating any file under src/test/java/ outside an explicit request or the gated execute-backend-test phase (this repo has no src/test tree at all). Add it when that phase runs. (2) TRANSACTION-PROPAGATION HALF, closed 2026-09-11 by the STEP 1.4 analysis's grounded candidate (a) — a REQUIRES_NEW entry point on NOTIF's crossmodule interface. Implemented as a NEW method NotificationDispatchApi.dispatchIndependently(DispatchCommand), delegating through NotificationDispatchApiImpl (the shared DispatchCommand → DispatchRequest mapping extracted into a private toRequest helper; dispatch's behaviour unchanged) to NOTIF's pre-existing DispatchService.dispatchSystem, which already declares @Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW). PasswordResetService.dispatchResetNotification now calls dispatchIndependently instead of dispatch, still inside InternalCallerContext and the existing catch-and-log, and its propagation comment states the new intent. This is exactly what build-create-service prescribes ("Cross-Module Calls"): REQUIRES_NEW "when the producing side performs a write that must commit independently of the caller's outcome". SEC could NOT call dispatchSystem directly — it is an internal @Service, and importing another module's @Service is an automatic-rejection trigger in gov-validate-backend-feature — so widening the existing crossmodule interface was the only sanctioned route. WHY NOT THE AFTER_COMMIT EVENT BRIDGE: rejected on the empirical finding already recorded in DispatchService.dispatchSystem's own javadoc — an AFTER_COMMIT @TransactionalEventListener "runs while the just-committed outer transaction's synchronization is still winding down, so the default REQUIRED propagation silently 'joins' it instead of opening a fresh one — isNewTransaction() comes back false, this method's own commit never fires, and the NOTIF_LOG row is dropped with no exception (confirmed empirically: the sequence advances, the row never appears)". A bridge would reintroduce the very failure REQUIRES_NEW exists to prevent. SIDE FIX, a live governance violation closed in passing: DispatchService.dispatchSystem carried NO @PreAuthorize while dispatch carried @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()") — an A.5.2 breach ("@PreAuthorize on EVERY public service method", on gov-validate-backend-feature's automatic-rejection list) that became reachable the moment SEC routed to it. dispatchSystem is now gated @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()"), which InternalCallerContext's synthetic principal satisfies exactly as it satisfies dispatch (verified by reading InternalCallerContext: the token is built with a non-empty authorities list, so it is authenticated and non-anonymous). Its javadoc's now-false "(the only caller)" clause — which named an AFTER_COMMIT listener as the sole caller — was corrected to name dispatchIndependently as the declared caller, and the REQUIRES_NEW rationale now states both independent reasons. Artifacts realigned: the API-SEC-003 Orchestration line in P3_1/backend-execution-plan-sec.md and its byte-identical packages/backend-execution/SVC-API/SVC-API-INT.md twin, and the PHASE 5 (INT-C) block in the plan and its packages/backend-execution/INT-C/INT-C.md twin (which no longer calls the caveat "gap #5"). P1/srs-sec.md needed no edit — verified: REQ-SEC-029/AC-SEC-029 say nothing about propagation and §A8 still classes Notifications as SOFT/optional; P2/db-script-sec.md needed none (no schema effect); test_gen/backend-test-plan-sec.md needed none — TC-SEC-006 and TC-SEC-029 assert only the 200, the token row and "one notification dispatch", none of which changes. OUTSTANDING, NOT DONE HERE, FLAGGED FOR A SEPARATE NOTIF PASS: NOTIF's OWN governance artifacts still owe a matching cross-module contract entry for the new interface method. governance/modules/NOTIF/** was deliberately NOT edited — a SEC-driven debate is not the authority to amend another module's artifacts. Specifically owed: (i) NOTIF's P3_1 backend-execution plan and its packages/backend-execution twin must document dispatchIndependently alongside dispatch on the NotificationDispatchApi surface, with its REQUIRES_NEW propagation, its isAuthenticated() gate and when a consumer should prefer it; (ii) the API-NOTIF-001 dispatch block must record that DispatchService.dispatchSystem is now reachable (indirectly) from outside NOTIF rather than being a purely internal in-JVM entry point, and that it is now @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()") gated; (iii) NOTIF's own execution-state.json should carry an entry for this interface widening and for the A.5.2 gate that was missing on dispatchSystem. Verified end to end after the change — the observed run is recorded against gap #9.

api_doc_gaps.detail: API-SEC-022's Response line names three quantities no SEC artifact defines. (a) recentActivity is "the last N AuditLogEntry" and N is never fixed — not in REQ-SEC-022/AC-SEC-022, not in SCR-REQ-SEC-007 B1-B5, not in prd-sec.md's dashboard story, not in db-script-sec.md. (b) rolesPermissionsSummary.privilegedRoleCount: "privileged" is defined nowhere in SEC v1 — srs-sec.md A3 ENT-SEC-002 has no privilege flag, A5 has no rule about it, and §7.1 / db-script-sec.md's 104 DBF carry no such column; the only adjacent statement is prd-sec.md:85's story text ("spot risk and over-privileged accounts at a glance"). (c) onboardingFunnel.stalledCount: no artifact says at what age a PENDING SignupRequest becomes stalled — SRS A7's SIGNUP_STATUS machine has no timeout, and the one DEFAULT-with-duration in the module (the 30-minute reset-token window) is scoped to ENT-SEC-012 only. backend-test-plan-sec.md's TC-SEC-022/TC-SEC-023 assert liveness and widget omission respectively and never assert any of the three values, so no test pins them either.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: Implemented with three named private static final constants in DashboardService, each carrying a comment saying the spec left the value open, and none of them promoted to a configuration property (no artifact authorizes one): RECENT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT = 10 entries, STALLED_SIGNUP_AGE = 7 days, and privilegedRoleCount read as RULE-SEC-007's own distinction — a role holding at least one action grant whose actionCode is not the VIEW gateway (QR-SEC-022 query RoleActionGrantRepository.countPrivilegedRoles, with the gateway code passed in as a parameter exactly as QR-SEC-030 already does). No table, column, route, error code, rule or config key was invented, and all three are confined to one class so a human decision can change them in one place. Remaining human-only question (a P1/P2 amendment, not an execution decision): whether SEC v1 should state N, a stalled-age threshold, and a definition of "privileged" for the dashboard, or drop the three figures from API-SEC-022's contract. Aligned 2026-09-11: the three operative definitions (N = 10, stalled = PENDING older than 7 days, privileged = holds at least one action grant whose actionCode is not the VIEW gateway) are now recorded as implementation-chosen defaults awaiting human confirmation, as a Notes line on API-SEC-022 in governance/modules/SEC/P3_1/backend-execution-plan-sec.md and packages/backend-execution/SVC-API/SVC-API-SEARCH.md, and as a Note field on REQ-SEC-022 in governance/modules/SEC/P1/srs-sec.md.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: api_docs_path — the published api-docs artifact has no producer in this repository
api_doc_gaps.detail: DOC.md (and the identical block in P3_1/backend-execution-plan-sec.md) states the frontend stage binds to "the real `api-docs-sec.md` published after implementation, never to this table", and execution-state.json's api_docs_path points at governance/modules/SEC/api-docs/. Neither can be satisfied as the repository stands. (a) governance/governance-tools/api-doc-generator/ extracts only from a live springdoc document; discovery.resolve() builds its URL as http://localhost:<port>/api-docs/<group-id> after matching --module against a GroupedOpenApi bean, and no GroupedOpenApi bean exists anywhere under src/main/java (verified by grep). `python3 generate.py --module SEC --function review` fails with "Could not identify a unique springdoc GroupedOpenApi group for module 'SEC'". (b) application.properties declares springdoc.api-docs.path=/v3/api-docs and no groups, so the single available document covers SEC, CU, NOTIF and FILE together — pointing --openapi at it would publish other modules' endpoints under modules/SEC/api-docs/. (c) the generator's output layout is index.md + endpoints/<group-slug>.md; it never produces a file named api-docs-sec.md, so that filename has no producer under any configuration. (d) no module in this repository has an api-docs/ directory at all (CU, FILE, FIN, MDL, NOTIF, SEC all checked), so there is no established pattern to mirror.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: CLOSED 2026-09-11 — on the human-authorized implementation of both decisions from the second-agent analysis. DECISION 1, per-module GroupedOpenApi beans in the app module: src/main/java/com/erp/main/config/OpenApiConfig.java (new, alongside JpaConfig and SecurityConfig) declares one bean per implemented module — secApi/`sec`, cuApi/`cu`, notifApi/`notif`, fileApi/`file` — each scanning that module's own controller package (com.erp.sec.controller, com.erp.cu.controller, com.erp.notif.controller, com.erp.file.controller — the four packages under src/main/java that actually hold @RestController classes). Grounding, read from the tool itself: discovery.py's header names "erp-main's GroupedOpenApi bean declarations for the springdoc group id, package(s), and display name that identify 'which module is ORG'", and discovery.match_openapi_group matches --module against the bean's method name / group id / display name. The group id is a published URL AND the generator's match key, so it must stay stable forever: it is the governance MODULE CODE lowercased, never a route prefix and never a package name — note that CU's live route prefix is /api/v1/common while its module code is CU, and the group id follows the code. Display names deliberately avoid the literal word "Security", because match_openapi_group is a substring test over normalised text and "security" contains "cu", which would make --module CU ambiguous between two groups and silently drop CU's source-derived sections. springdoc.api-docs.path and server.port in application.properties were NOT changed. Verified live after a clean compile and restart: GET /v3/api-docs 200 with 46 paths (the aggregate document is unchanged), GET /v3/api-docs/sec 200 with 25 paths, all of them /api/v1/sec; /v3/api-docs/swagger-config now lists four urls[] entries where it previously listed none. DECISION 2, the generator's output layout is authoritative and `api-docs-sec.md` is struck from the plan. All three grounding claims re-verified against the real files: renderers/markdown_renderer.render() returns {"index.md": ...} plus one "endpoints/<group-slug>.md" per group and nothing else; discovery.default_output_dir returns the DIRECTORY governance/modules/<MOD>/api-docs, which is exactly what api_docs_path already names; and the repo-root CLAUDE.md ownership table lists api-docs/ as a folder, not a file. Amended accordingly, structure preserved: the DOC-phase "API contract summary" paragraph now binds the frontend stage to "the real generated api-docs published under governance/modules/SEC/api-docs/ ... index.md plus endpoints/<group-slug>.md" at P3_1/backend-execution-plan-sec.md:1115 and its byte-identical twin packages/backend-execution/DOC/DOC.md:6 (_SECTIONS.md carries no DOC block, so it needed no edit for this). The only surviving api-docs-sec.md string outside this entry's own detail field is governance/modules/FIN/_state/briefs/test-gen-project.md:6455, an archived FIN-owned brief holding a copy of the same sentence — deliberately NOT touched. api_doc_gaps.endpoint: XM-INBOUND-GAP-1 — no SEC endpoint returns a role's user set (inbound contract assumed by FIN)
api_doc_gaps.detail: governance/modules/FIN/P3_1/backend-execution-plan-fin.md:383-386 states that RULE-FIN-015's separation-of-duties check "runs in FIN's own service layer by reading the two roles' user sets through SEC's role/grant read APIs". Verified against the 27 implemented SEC endpoints: RoleGrantController exposes writes only (POST /roles/{id}/modules, DELETE /roles/{id}/modules/{moduleId}, POST /roles/{id}/screens, POST /roles/{id}/actions) and no GET; RoleController exposes only POST /roles/search (RoleResponse carries role attributes, no member list) and POST /roles; UserController has no GET /users/{id}/roles (only PUT /users/{id}/roles), and POST /users/search accepts filters on username, email, fullName and statusCode only (UserService.ALLOWED_SORT_FIELDS / UserSearchRequest adds no role predicate); API-SEC-027 (GET /api/v1/sec/menu) is caller-self-scoped — MenuController takes no input at all and resolves the caller from the session — and returns ModuleMenuResponse (modules -> screens), never another user's grants and never an effective-action list. FIN's stated mechanism therefore has no SEC surface to call.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: CLOSED 2026-09-11 — and not by either candidate this entry first listed. The second-agent analysis converged on a better THIRD answer, which the human authorized: not a new SEC REST endpoint (candidate a) and not an amendment to FIN's mechanism (candidate b), but a narrow cross-module Spring interface. The grounding is binding skill text, not preference — .claude/skills/build-create-service/SKILL.md "Cross-Module Calls": "Modules are package-by-feature areas inside one deployable — always deployed together. Cross-module reads go through direct Spring interface injection, not loopback HTTP." Adding a REST endpoint so FIN could call SEC over HTTP would therefore have been the one shape the skill forbids, which is why the original finding (no SEC ENDPOINT returns a role's user set) stands as written and no endpoint was added. BUILT, per the same skill's "Exposing this module to others": src/main/java/com/erp/sec/crossmodule/ — SecUserDirectoryApi (the narrow interface), UserContact (its read-model record) and SecUserDirectoryApiImpl (a small @Component delegating to UserService, injecting no repository, so the exposed surface stays narrower than the internal service). api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/sec/auth/logout — self-service session termination (ENT-SEC-010) — no API-SEC id exists for one
api_doc_gaps.detail: SVC-API-INT.md declares API-SEC-001 (login) as the only entry on this session's lifecycle; API-SEC-026 exists but is the ADMINISTRATOR-initiated termination of someone else's session (PERM_SEC_SESSIONS_TERMINATE), not a caller ending their own. A signed-in user therefore had no server-side way to end their own session before its natural expiry — a frontend logout could only discard the token locally, leaving the ActiveSession row (and the token itself, until expiry) live. Published POST /api/v1/sec/auth/logout: resolves the caller's own session from their bearer token's jti (DBF-SEC-077, the same field API-SEC-026 keys on) rather than accepting a session id in the body — a client-supplied id would make this API-SEC-026 without its administrator gate. Gated on isAuthenticated() only, no permission, since a caller can only ever end their own session. Idempotent: a session already carrying terminatedAt is returned as-is rather than raising SEC-409-ALREADY-TERMINATED, which stays reserved for API-SEC-026 telling an administrator someone else's session was already closed. Writes one LOGOUT audit row per actual termination (none on the idempotent repeat). Ported from a sibling branch's implementation, which had annotated the code with its own forward-looking ids (API-SEC-028, REQ-SEC-036, AC-SEC-036, DBF-SEC-081/082) — none of those exist in this module's governance plan; they are code comments, not assigned contract ids, and are flagged here rather than treated as authoritative. Verified against the running app and by SecLogoutIntegrationTest (3 cases: own-session-only termination + audit row, the token rejected by JwtAuthenticationFilter afterwards, and idempotency on repeat).
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED — implemented in this repo 2026-09-18. The factory still owns assigning it a real API-SEC id and a contract line in SVC-API-INT.md, and should reconcile or discard the code's own invented API-SEC-028/REQ-SEC-036/AC-SEC-036/DBF-SEC-081/082 references once a real id lands.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: GET /api/v1/sec/roles/{id} and GET /api/v1/sec/users/{id} — the single-resource read of ENT-SEC-002 and ENT-SEC-001; no API-SEC id exists for either
api_doc_gaps.detail: SVC-API-CRUD.md publishes search (API-SEC-005/012), create, update and the status transitions for both entities, but no read-one. Both paths therefore answered 405 — the path existed, GET was not published. The frontend E2E second pass (sec-frontend-e2e-run-2026-09-18.md) reported the consequence: its roles screen drives the edit drawer from the URL (/security/roles?editId=7), which MANDATE F4-RULE-7 requires, and on a COLD load the drawer could not resolve the row because a client can only see roles inside the page of search results it happens to have loaded. The drawer was deep-linkable only within a session that had already listed the row, and the same absence is why neither entity has a detail screen (their ADR-SEC-008). Published the ordinary read for each: 200 with exactly the RoleResponse / UserResponse the corresponding search already returns (for users, including the roles array added in round 1, resolved through UserRoleService.rolesOf), 404 SEC-404-ROLE / SEC-404-USER for an unknown id, gated on PERM_SEC_ROLES_VIEW / PERM_SEC_USERS_VIEW — the same permission as the search, since this exposes no field the search does not. No new DTO, no new error code, no schema change. GET /api/v1/sec/signup-requests/{id} was deliberately NOT added: it also answers 405, but the frontend has no use for it and an unrequested endpoint is a contract surface nobody owns. Verified against the running app (roles/7 and users/636 both 200 with the full response; unknown ids 404 with the right codes) and by SecReadOneIntegrationTest (4 cases: both happy paths, the users one asserting the roles array, and both 404s).
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED — implemented in this repo 2026-09-18. The factory owns assigning each a real API-SEC id and a contract line in SVC-API-CRUD.md; it may also want to decide whether the read-one is a standing part of the CRUD package for every entity, since its absence here was not a considered omission but a gap that only surfaced once a screen deep-linked a row.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/sec/dev/password-reset-token — a dev-profile test fixture, NOT a contract endpoint and it must never be assigned an API-SEC id
api_doc_gaps.detail: TC-SEC-038 (complete a reset with a VALID token) was unreachable by any automated run. Its negative half passes (an expired/invalid token is refused with SEC-409-RESET-TOKEN-INVALID) and API-SEC-003 passes including its no-enumeration property, but nothing could read the raw token API-SEC-003 issues: PasswordResetService persists only the SHA-256 hash, and the raw value leaves the process in the mail and nowhere else. Added a @Profile("dev") controller + service that mints a token for a given email and returns the raw value — same entity, same TokenHasher, same A7 30-minute window, but no mail and no PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED audit row, because it is a fixture and not a second implementation of API-SEC-003. Containment is the profile: outside dev the bean does not exist, so neither does the path. It additionally requires an authenticated caller (SecurityConfig's permitAll list names only the four pre-authentication endpoints), which is why revealing whether an address is registered here does not weaken API-SEC-003's no-enumeration property. Verified on a dev instance end to end (issue → complete → 200, and reusing the spent token → 409 SEC-409-RESET-TOKEN-INVALID) and on a prod-profile instance, where the path has no handler while GET /roles/{id} still answers 200; SecReadOneIntegrationTest covers the issue-then-complete round trip and the unknown-email 404.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN — the factory should decide whether a dev-only test fixture belongs in the delivered source at all, or whether the governed way to reach TC-SEC-038 is a Dev/Test mail catcher (MailHog) declared as environment rather than code. The implementation here is the cheapest of the three options the frontend offered and is reversible; it is flagged rather than treated as settled because it is the first non-contract endpoint in this module.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: RULE-SEC-005 / SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT (API-SEC-008, API-SEC-017) — dormant, and confirmed dormant by design
api_doc_gaps.detail: The frontend E2E second pass asked whether the segregation-of-duties guard is intentionally inert. It is, and nothing was changed. RULE-SEC-005 forbids one user holding both actions of a module-declared conflicting pair; both guards are live (UserRoleService.holdsConflictingAction on assignment, RoleGrantService.anyUserOfRoleHoldsConflictingAction on grant) and both route through their Domain objects to SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT, but conflictingCounterpartActions() resolves empty because SEC v1 declares no conflicting-pair source anywhere and the platform's only real pair is FIN-owned and FIN-enforced (governance/modules/FIN/P3_1/backend-execution-plan-fin.md:1061-1066). The frontend guard is live on both its paths too, so the rule is fully wired end to end with nothing to trigger it. TC-SEC-050 (frontend) and TC-SEC-020 (backend) are therefore unreachable-by-design, not gaps, and the answer given to the frontend was (a) intentionally dormant — no Dev conflicting pair will be declared to make them fire, because a fabricated pair would test the plumbing against a fact the platform does not assert.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN — no code change requested or made. The factory owns the real decision: either declare where a conflicting action pair comes from (a SEC-owned registry table, or a per-module declaration SEC reads), or state in the plan that RULE-SEC-005 stays dormant in v1 so TC-SEC-020/TC-SEC-050 can be recorded as unreachable-by-design instead of being re-reported as gaps every run.
